description:
## Problem
#4437 removed three unenforced timer keys but, by scope, left two dead config surfaces:
- `execution.timeout_minutes` (default 120) is set in `SimpleConfigProvider` defaults (benchbox/utils/config_interface.py) but has no reader outside tests. Like the removed keys, it promises a limit nothing enforces.
- `ExecutionConfigHelper.optimize_for_system` (benchbox/utils/config_helpers.py) keeps a `memory_gb` parameter it no longer uses.

## Owner decisions
For the three keys removed in #4437 (2026-11-20): "re-verify that nothing enforces them, then remove all three and say so in the breaking-change changelog entry. A config file that still sets one gets a clear message pointing to `execution.timeout_seconds`." The owner asked for this follow-up on 2026-11-22. Removed-key message, verbatim: "`{key}` is no longer used and has no effect. Use `execution.timeout_seconds` to limit a run."

## Change
1. Re-verify on current develop, with language-server references (or jedi plus an AST scan if no language server is available) and grep over benchbox/, scripts/, docs/, examples/, that nothing reads or enforces `execution.timeout_minutes` and that no caller passes `memory_gb`; list the evidence.
2. If unread, remove the key and its default and add it to `REMOVED_CONFIG_KEYS` in benchbox/cli/config.py so a config file that sets it gets the message above; remove the unused `memory_gb` parameter and update its callers.
3. One breaking-change changelog fragment naming the key (and the parameter if public).

## Decision gates
- A real reader or caller (its own tests do not count): STOP, keep it, and record what reads it on this item.
- The message text is the owner's, verbatim.

## Verification rubric
The references evidence is in the pull request; a test loads a config file setting `execution.timeout_minutes` and gets the message without crashing (fails before); `optimize_for_system` callers still pass; `make duplicate-check-delta` and `make pr-preflight` exit 0.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`), never the primary clone. Edit files with the edit tool, never by script. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, UAT, generators at scale) only through `make heavy-run` or lock-taking entry points; never skip the lock, admission or watchdog; never delete anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. No live cloud run and no cloud credentials unless this item's Decision gates say the owner approved it in the current task. BenchBox imposes no default run limit: add none. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; one changelog fragment for a user-facing change. Never post a stand-in review, close and reopen a pull request to restart CI, use `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite an author. Arm once; a second time only after fixing the cause the refusal named. Reply on every review thread; resolve it only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise it again.
